methodology: Both candidates measured on the SAME 4 real development cases (P6-D1/D2/D3/D8), same real Evidence, same frozen Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b model - only the architecture differs (Candidate A: free-form prose + regex-parsed [[evidence_id]] markers; Candidate B: strict-JSON-schema structured claim list). Candidate B was additionally measured on all 13 dev+validation cases (see artifacts/v2/phase6_validation_results.json) since it is the contract's provisionally-favored architecture per Section 6's schema-reliability preference; Candidate A was measured on this smaller comparison subset only, sufficient to surface a real, reproducible qualitative defect (below) that motivates NOT building the more complex Candidate C.
real_findings: Candidate A leaked its own internal evidence_id namespace string into user-facing prose on case P6-D3 ('...although the evidence records are associated with the identifier chembl:CHEMBL941.') - the free-form prose architecture has no structural barrier preventing the model from writing an internal ID token directly into visible text, unlike Candidate B where evidence_id never appears in any user-facing field (only in the structured evidence_ids array, consumed by the deterministic compiler, never rendered as literal text).

Candidate A failed to preserve the raw ClinicalTrials phase enum value verbatim on P6-D2 (wrote natural-sounding 'Phase 2' instead of the raw field value 'PHASE2'), while Candidate B's structured extraction copied the raw value exactly - a real, reproducible difference in source-fidelity discipline between the two architectures, not a one-off.

Candidate B passed 10/10 real development cases and 3/3 real validation cases (see phase6_validation_results.json) with zero unknown-Evidence-ID references, zero fabricated content, and correct abstention/conflict handling across all tested categories.

decision: SELECTED: candidate_b_structured. Reasons: (1) structural safety - the strict JSON schema makes an evidence_id leak into visible prose structurally impossible, whereas Candidate A's free-form architecture demonstrably leaked one on real data; (2) source fidelity - Candidate B preserved raw structured field values verbatim where Candidate A naturalized them, which matters for any downstream exact-value consumer; (3) Candidate B met all predeclared hard gates and all measured dev+validation cases with a single Cerebras call, the same cost/latency class as Candidate A. Candidate C (claim-plan + composition, a second LLM call) was NOT built: no defect found in Candidate B's dev/validation results motivates the added latency/cost/complexity of a second-stage call, per directive Step 27's 'do not build Candidate C merely because it sounds sophisticated.'
